mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 4.3% triggers a loss of labor market confidence, reducing expected corporate earnings growth and thereby decreasing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite UNRATE crossing the 4.3% threshold, or t-test p-value > 0.05 in a 12-month window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in billings (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) signal robust demand growth, which amplifies investor optimism and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: both GDPC1 and RSAFS increase in the same month
failure_condition: The combined effect of GDPC1 and RSAFS does not significantly predict higher returns (p > 0.05 in a 6-month window).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, rising industrial production (INDPRO) and CPI inflation both indicate overcapacity and muted growth expectations, compressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: both INDPRO and CPIAUCSL rise above 101.4 and 324.4 respectively in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in such periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05 over 18 months).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1200 units signals weakening demand, leading to reduced corporate investment and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls below 1200 units in a month
failure_condition: 5-day returns remain positive despite HOUST crossing the 1200 threshold, or p-value > 0.05 in a 6-month window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment (PAYEMS) alongside higher federal funds rates signal tight labor markets and restrictive monetary policy, dampening equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: both PAYEMS and FEDFUNDS increase in the same month
failure_condition: The combined effect of PAYEMS and FEDFUNDS does not significantly predict negative returns (p > 0.05 in a 12-month window).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in industrial production (INDPRO) reflects robust supply chain activity, boosting investor confidence and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05 over 3 years).

mechanism_narrative: In a post-shock recovery, falling unemployment (UNRATE below 4.0%) coupled with rising federal funds rates (above 3.5%) signals policy normalization and stronger growth prospects, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.0% and FEDFUNDS rise above 3.5% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day returns fail to rise significantly above baseline (p > 0.05 in a 24-month window).
